rationale:
The two {test} items cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits`.

**One entry per enclosing item, even with several hits.**
- `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration` searches `const A ... "éhit"; const B ... "hit hit";`.
- `const B` contains two hits. The raw `search_text` results show three hits, two of them in `code.rs#const[B]`.
- The dispatched `search_text` page asserts exactly two entries: `tag` "1" for A and `tag` "2" for B. B has a single entry.
- `search_pages_return_every_original_match_in_order` writes 350 lines of `hit {i} hit`, so each line has two hits. It asserts one entry per node, in order, with `count == lines.len()`.

**Group before pagination, so an item's excerpt stays together.**
- The 350-line test asserts `pages > 1`, so it spans several pages. Every entry on every page equals `{"node":nodes[count], "excerpt":lines[count], "tag":...}`.
- If grouping happened after pagination, a two-hit item could be split across a page boundary. That would give a duplicate or partial entry and break the `nodes[count]` and `count` assertions.
- I read `dispatch` in `project_sources.rs` and the `chunks` function in `pages.rs`. Grouping runs in `dispatch` before `pages.search`, and pages are chunked from the grouped entries.
- The exact page boundary depends on the page size and entry sizes, so the test would catch a split only if a boundary fell inside a two-hit item. This is a weaker point, but the test does span many pages with multi-hit items.

**Each entry carries a node reference, one excerpt, and a page-local tag.**
- Entries are compared as whole JSON objects containing `node`, `excerpt`, and `tag`.
- Tags restart at `(index+1)` on every page, which checks that they are page-local.
- The excerpt for B is the whole declaration `const B: &str = "hit hit";`, so it covers both hits.
- The node value equals the interned node ID of the raw hit.

**The tag accounts for use of the excerpt.**
- `finish_search` with `used: []` yields no dependencies.
- `finish_search` with `used: ["2"]` yields `Dependency::Node(code.rs#const[B], fingerprint)`.

**Node reference lets the agent read the full item.**
- `session.read_node` on the page's second match yields a `Dependency::Node` for B's node.
- The format of the node reference is the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`. I did not reassess it, as the task directs.

I found no unacknowledged gap. There were no {fixme} acknowledgments.

text: Deliver one entry per enclosing item in a text search, even when the item has several hits. Group before pagination so an item's excerpt stays together. Each entry carries a node reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`, one excerpt, and the page-local tag used by `finish_search`. The tag accounts for use of the excerpt. The node reference lets the agent read the full item.

The agent harness uses the unsigned integer representation of `NodeId<D>` for the current node, supplied inputs, and nodes in tool results. Built-in tools accepting a node ID resolve that integer in the domain's cache. A malformed value or an unassigned integer produces a tool error before any graph read.
For example, if a search hit contains `"node": 7`, the agent can call `read_node({"node": 7})` to read the enclosing node.
